title: San León Magno : el Papa que defendió la fe y la civilización cristiana – INFOVATICANA
summary: El “Tomus ad Flavianum”: piedra angular del dogma cristológico León Magno fue un teólogo de precisión y profundidad extraordinarias. Su famosa carta doctrinal al patriarca Flaviano de Constantinopla —
content: El “Tomus ad Flavianum”: piedra angular del dogma cristológico León Magno fue un teólogo de precisión y profundidad extraordinarias. Su famosa carta doctrinal al patriarca Flaviano de Constantinopla —conocida como el Tomus ad Flavianum— definió con claridad la doctrina católica sobre las dos naturalezas de Cristo: divina y humana, unidas en una sola Persona. Este documento fue leído en el Concilio de Calcedonia (451) ante cientos de obispos que, al escucharlo, exclamaron: “Pedro ha hablado por boca de León.” Con esa expresión, la Iglesia universal reconocía el primado de la sede romana y la continuidad entre el Apóstol Pedro y sus sucesores. En tiempos en que el poder imperial pretendía someter la doctrina al control político, León reivindicó que la autoridad del Papa no depende del César ni de los concilios, sino de Cristo mismo, que prometió: “Tú eres Pedro, y sobre esta piedra edificaré mi Iglesia.” Gracias a su intervención, el Concilio de Calcedonia se convirtió en un hito de la ortodoxia cristológica y en un testimonio de la primacía del Romano Pontífice. El Papa León no impuso su autoridad con la fuerza, sino con la verdad; no por ambición humana, sino por fidelidad al depósito recibido. El Papa que detuvo a Atila En el año 452, la amenaza de los hunos llegó hasta las puertas de Italia. Atila, llamado “el azote de Dios”, había devastado Europa central y avanzaba hacia Roma. Sin ejército ni armas, León decidió ir al encuentro del invasor acompañado solo de algunos clérigos. El encuentro en el río Mincio, cerca de Mantua, se convirtió en uno de los episodios más sobrecogedores de la historia. La tradición narra que Atila, al ver al Papa, quedó sobrecogido por una fuerza sobrenatural y decidió retirarse. Algunos cronistas antiguos dicen que el caudillo vio detrás de León a los santos Pedro y Pablo empuñando espadas. Fuera cual fuera la causa, el hecho histórico es indiscutible: el Papa, solo con su autoridad moral, salvó a Roma de una destrucción segura. Tres años después, en el 455, León volvió a intervenir ante el vándalo Genserico, quien, aunque saqueó la ciudad, accedió a no incendiarla ni matar a sus habitantes. En una era de barbarie y desesperanza, el Papa se convirtió en defensor de la dignidad humana y de la civilización cristiana naciente. Un pastor de almas y doctor de la fe Más allá de los hechos históricos, el legado espiritual de León Magno se encuentra en sus Sermones y Cartas, textos que combinan rigor teológico, belleza retórica y profundidad pastoral. Sus homilías sobre la Encarnación y la Pascua son verdaderas joyas del pensamiento cristiano. En ellas resuena una teología que no separa la doctrina de la vida, ni la fe de la caridad. Fue también un reformador eclesial: disciplinó al clero, combatió los abusos, promovió la vida monástica y fortaleció la autoridad episcopal. Instituyó la solemnidad de la Natividad del Señor en Roma y consolidó la liturgia romana, que más tarde se extendería a toda la cristiandad. En un tiempo en que el caos amenazaba con disolver las instituciones, León mostró que la verdadera reforma de la Iglesia comienza en la santidad de sus pastores. De su espiritualidad brota una enseñanza perenne: el cristiano no puede dejarse arrastrar por el miedo ni por la confusión del mundo. Como escribió en una de sus homilías más célebres: “Reconoce, cristiano, tu dignidad. Y, puesto que has sido hecho partícipe de la naturaleza divina, no vuelvas a la antigua vileza con una conducta indigna.” En esas palabras se resume toda su visión: la fe no es una idea, sino una transformación de la persona; una participación real en la vida de Cristo. El Doctor que iluminó siglos León Magno murió el 10 de noviembre del año 461. Fue sepultado en la Basílica de San Pedro y proclamado Doctor de la Iglesia en el siglo XVIII por el Papa Benedicto XIV. Su influencia doctrinal se extendió por siglos y moldeó el pensamiento cristiano sobre el sacerdocio, la autoridad papal y la teología de la Encarnación. Su magi

title: Quando o escutismo católico deixa de ser católico
summary: 1.A Associação de Guias e Escuteiros Católicos Italianos (AGECI) eliminou, muito recentemente, a orientação sexual e a identidade de género como critérios de recrutamento e selecção daqueles que prete
content: 1.A Associação de Guias e Escuteiros Católicos Italianos (AGECI) eliminou, muito recentemente, a orientação sexual e a identidade de género como critérios de recrutamento e selecção daqueles que pretendem, no âmbito da missão do adulto no escutismo, exercer responsabilidades educativas. É uma decisão relevante, que suscita reflexão e debate. O que está em causa não é uma mera alteração administrativa ou organizativa, nem uma actualização do sistema de progresso ou do uniforme. O que está em causa é algo estruturante, que tem a ver com a própria natureza e essência do Movimento Escutista, em particular do Escutismo Católico. A questão não é saber se pessoas com atracção pelo mesmo sexo podem ou não fazer parte de um agrupamento; não se pretende indagar da vida íntima dos membros, nem perseguir ou excluir alguém por causa da sua orientação. A igual dignidade de todos os seres humanos, criados à imagem de Deus, constitui um valor inegociável. A questão que se coloca é outra: que modelo de ser humano o Escutismo Católico propõe às crianças e aos adolescentes através dos seus educadores; e isto sim, é algo que nos deve interpelar profundamente. 2. Todo o processo educativo, também no escutismo, não é neutro ou vazio de sentidos; tem sempre por base uma determinada visão do Homem, da Sociedade e do mundo, ou seja, uma determinada cosmovisão, neste caso, cristã. É por isso que adquire enorme importância garantir que os grandes documentos orientadores do escutismo católico sejam, em toda a sua pedagogia, permeados pela visão cristã do Homem e da sociedade. E é igualmente importante garantir, naquilo que humanamente é possível garantir, que os Chefes, enquanto educadores chamados a levar a cabo essa missão, tenham o perfil adequado para tão elevada tarefa. É por isso que vemos com perplexidade e apreensão que uma importante organização que se apresenta como católica renuncie explicitamente a avaliar a adequação antropológica e moral daqueles que se tornarão referências para crianças e adolescentes, precisamente numa idade em que procuram exemplos e modelos para além da esfera estritamente familiar. 3. Não se trata de questionar a dignidade pessoal de quem quer que seja, que é inegável e deve sempre ser respeitada. Como recorda o Catecismo da Igreja Católica, as pessoas com tendências homossexuais devem ser acolhidas com respeito, compaixão e delicadeza, ee para com elas toda a forma de discriminação injusta (cf. CEC 2358-2359). Importa por isso distinguir com clareza três planos: a pessoa, sempre digna de acolhimento; a tendência ou atracção, que não é em si mesma culpa moral; e os comportamentos e opções de vida livremente assumidos e publicamente testemunhadovitando-ss. A questão que se coloca a um movimento da Igreja não é a da dignidade da pessoa, mas a da coerência do testemunho educativo: são aceitáveis, em quem educa em nome da Igreja, comportamentos, opções e estilos de vida assumidos de forma estável e declarada em conflito com a visão cristã da sexualidade? A orientação sexual ou a identidade de género não podem ser consideradas irrelevantes para o discernimento educativo sem se assumir implicitamente que a antropologia católica sobre o homem, a mulher, a sua igual dignidade, complementaridade e reciprocidade, seria irrelevante. Esta exigência de clareza moral e de coerência de vida não se dirige apenas a pessoas homossexuais; dirige-se a todos os educadores, heterossexuais incluídos, chamados à castidade segundo o próprio estado de vida, à fidelidade matrimonial, ao respeito pela vida nascente e a uma afectividade ordenada. Só assim podem constituir-se como modelos credíveis para os jovens, ajudando-os a construir de forma integrada a sua personalidade e identidade. É isto que credibiliza e dá coerência ao método escutista enquanto movimento educativo, e que lhe confere uma sabedoria, uma mística e uma identidade propriamente católicas. 4. Vivemos um tempo em que proliferam ideias que se assemelham à fé, que usam o seu vocab

title: El papa León XIV ya está en Argentina y el campo tuvo protagonismo en su primer discurso
summary: Tras pasar por Uruguay, el papa León XIV inició este domingo su histórica gira de cuatro días por Argentina, que constituye la primera llegada de un líder de la Iglesia Católica mundial a nuestro país
content: Tras pasar por Uruguay, el papa León XIV inició este domingo su histórica gira de cuatro días por Argentina, que constituye la primera llegada de un líder de la Iglesia Católica mundial a nuestro país desde Juan Pablo II en 1987. En ese marco, la primera actividad del Sumo Pontífice fue un discurso en el Palacio Libertad de la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires (CABA), frente al presidente de la Nación, Javier Milei. Y aunque sus palabras lógicamente estuvieron apuntadas hacia toda la sociedad, hubo numerosos pasajes que encontraron especial sintonía con el mundo agropecuario. Esto, en la previa de la reunión que León XIV mantendrá el lunes con representantes empresariales, sindicales y de organizaciones sociales, entre los que estarán los presidentes de las cuatro entidades de la Mesa de Enlace. EL PAPA LEÓN XIV EN ARGENTINA Puntualmente, el jefe mayor del Vaticano destacó el valor del esfuerzo cotidiano de los argentinos, con una mención expresa a quienes trabajan en el campo, y reivindicó la importancia de generar oportunidades, estimular la iniciativa privada y aprovechar responsablemente los recursos naturales. “Esta tierra conoce bien el valor del esfuerzo de quienes se ganan la vida en el campo y en las ciudades”, expresó León XIV, al destacar también el papel de los emprendedores y de las familias que sostienen sus hogares a través del trabajo. Asimismo, el Papa reconoció el enorme potencial productivo del país, al señalar que la Argentina cuenta con una extraordinaria riqueza natural, desde sus campos y reservas de agua hasta sus fuentes de energía, minerales y biodiversidad. Así, su mensaje combinó la posibilidad de aprovechar esos recursos para generar desarrollo y bienestar con la responsabilidad de preservar el ambiente y las condiciones de vida de las futuras generaciones. También dedicó un espacio a la innovación, la investigación y las nuevas tecnologías, incluida la inteligencia artificial, destacando su capacidad para transformar la producción y mejorar la vida de las personas. Por otro lado, al expresar una mirada sobre América del Sur, mencionó además a los alimentos, la energía y el conocimiento como elementos que vinculan a los países y abren oportunidades para fortalecer la cooperación regional. LEON XIV, EL MARTÍN FIERO Y EL MATE Asimismo, León XIV ofreció referencias cargadas de simbolismo para la identidad argentina. Por ejemplo, mencionó al Martín Fierro de José Hernández, a Jorge Luis Borges, al tango y a las tradiciones del interior del país. Y no faltó una de las costumbres más arraigadas entre los argentinos: el mate compartido, al que presentó como un gesto cotidiano que favorece la conversación y la cercanía. Por último, hacia el final de su intervención, León XIV evocó a Nuestra Señora de Luján, patrona de la Argentina y figura de especial significado para las comunidades rurales y para generaciones de familias de todo el país. También recordó al papa Francisco, citó a Carlos Gardel y alentó a los argentinos a valorar el patrimonio recibido de las generaciones anteriores y trabajar para dejar un país mejor a quienes vendrán. De esta manera, sin ser un discurso específicamente dirigido al agro, las palabras de León XIV dejaron un reconocimiento al trabajo rural, a la producción, a la iniciativa emprendedora y a las tradiciones que forman parte de la identidad argentina. Un mensaje que también llegó al corazón del campo argentino. EL DISCURSO COMPLETO DEL PAPA LEÓN XIV Señor Presidente de la República, distinguidas autoridades y miembros del cuerpo diplomático. Señoras y señores, me alegra profundamente encontrarme hoy en esta querida tierra argentina. Agradezco, señor Presidente, las cordiales palabras que ha tenido a bien dirigirme y la acogida que por medio de usted me brinda su pueblo. Saludos también a los miembros del cuerpo diplomático y a las demás autoridades aquí presentes, y extiendo con afecto mi saludo a todos los argentinos. title: Papa Leone : Lautorità intesa come servizio è orientata al bene comune
summary: Primo discorso della seconda tappa del viaggio apostolico di Papa Leone XIV in Sud America. Parlando al Palacio Libertad a Buenos Aires, di fronte alle autorità, alla società civile e al corpo diploma
content: Primo discorso della seconda tappa del viaggio apostolico di Papa Leone XIV in Sud America. Parlando al Palacio Libertad a Buenos Aires, di fronte alle autorità, alla società civile e al corpo diplomatico argentini, il Santo Padre ha ricordato che ogni generazione riceve ine eredità dalla precedente il proprio Paese e a sua volta partecipa alla sua costruzione, imparando a discernere cosa va conservato. Il patrimonio comune, ha aggiunto Leone, comprende anche la democrazia, che chiede all’autorità di intendere il proprio compito come servizio orientato al bene comune a partire dalle condizioni concrete della vita delle persone, come le famiglie e i giovani, che devono poter ricevere opportunità professionali ed educazione per realizzare i propri progetti di vita senza il peso dell’incertezza o dover andare altrove. Il saluto “Signor Presidente della Repubblica, distinte Autorità e membri del Corpo diplomatico, Signore e Signori,sono molto lieto di trovarmi oggi in questa cara Terra argentina. La ringrazio, Signor Presidente, per le cordiali parole che ha voluto rivolgermi e per l’accoglienza che, attraverso di Lei, mi riserva il suo Popolo. Saluto inoltre i membri del Corpo diplomatico e le altre Autorità presenti, ed estendo con affetto il mio saluto a tutti gli Argentini. “Sono venuto come Successore dell’Apostolo Pietro e, pertanto, come Pastore. Desidero incontrare la Chiesa in cammino in questa Terra e rivolgermi anche all’intera Nazione e a coloro ai quali è stato affidato il compito di servirla. La Chiesa accompagna la vita dei popoli attraverso la missione che le è stata affidata. Per questo, anche nei confronti di coloro che ricoprono cariche pubbliche, desidera offrire una parola ispirata al Vangelo e volta a tutelare la dignità di ogni persona, la concordia e il bene comune“. Un’ampia storia “Venire in questa terra ha, per me, un significato particolare. Per dodici anni la Chiesa universale ha ascoltato la voce di un Pontefice argentino, che ha portato con sé, nella memoria e nel cuore, i luoghi, le persone e la fede che qui ha ricevuto. Oggi, succedendogli nel Ministero petrino, percorro in un certo senso la strada inversa e vengo nella Patria dove Papa Francesco ha iniziato un cammino, che in seguito si sarebbe intrecciato con quello di tutta la Chiesa. Avvicinarmi alla terra in cui è cresciuto significa anche avvicinarmi a una storia molto più ampia, fatta di generazioni di uomini e donne che, prima e dopo di lui, hanno accolto questa Patria e vi hanno lasciato qualcosa di sé. Alcuni sono nati qui; altri sono giunti da lontano e vi hanno trovato una casa; altri ancora appartengono a popoli indigeni, la cui presenza precede la nascita della Nazione. Da quell’incontro fra origini ed esperienze diverse ha preso forma, col passare del tempo, un Popolo che ha saputo aprire le proprie porte, fare spazio a chi arrivava e mantenere, anche nei momenti difficili, una notevole capacità di rialzarsi e andare avanti. Tutti hanno contribuito a plasmare l’Argentina che oggi ho la gioia di visitare”. Il patrimonio comune “Nessuna generazione costruisce la Patria partendo da zero. La riceve. Lo fa attraverso una lingua e legami che l’hanno preceduta; attraverso istituzioni fondate da altri e beni che sono cresciuti grazie al lavoro di molti. La storia custodisce motivi di gratitudine, ma anche ricordi dolorosi. Spetta a ogni generazione discernere ciò che merita di essere conservato, affrontare le conseguenze ingiuste del passato e accrescere il patrimonio materiale e spirituale comune. La patria che oggi è nelle vostre mani sarà domani l’eredità di altri”. Unica memoria collettiva “La cultura offre alcune delle manifestazioni più caratteristiche di tale lascito, e l’Argentina ha saputo esprimersi con una voce riconoscibile ben oltre i propri confini: nel Martín Fierro di José Hernández; nelle pagine di Jorge Luis Borges e di tanti scrittori che hanno arricchito la lingua spagnola con accenti del Río de la Plata; nel tango, nato

title: Why Did Prosecutors Agree To Omit References to Katy Perry From the Opening Statements at Trial ?
summary: Prosecutors agreed to remove references to Katy Perry from their opening statement at Russell Brand's London rape trial after objections from his lawyers. The decision emerged on Thursday, 5 November
content: Prosecutors agreed to remove references to Katy Perry from their opening statement at Russell Brand's London rape trial after objections from his lawyers. The decision emerged on Thursday, 5 November 2026, after a jury returned verdicts at Southwark Crown Court. Brand, 51, was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women. Jurors acquitted him of two further rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault. He had denied all seven charges, which concerned six women. Details of the pretrial discussions became public after reporting restrictions ended. They showed how Brand's former marriage was kept out of the prosecution's opening address, although he later mentioned Perry while giving evidence. Why Katy Perry References Were Removed From the Opening Lead prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC acknowledged in written submissions that references to Brand's relationship with Perry after 2009 'may be sensitive'. According to Sky News' court reporting, prosecutors were 'content to remove these from the opening' following defence submissions. The agreement was limited to the opening statement. It did not prevent every mention of Perry during the proceedings or establish that the relationship itself was evidence of wrongdoing. Perry was not accused of any offence. Prosecutors also agreed to leave out references to Brand's earlier religious beliefs and his 2024 baptism. His Christian conversion was nevertheless mentioned during questioning of his wife, Laura, showing that the restrictions on the opening did not cover all subsequent testimony. Other arguments before the trial concerned references to Brand's past drug and alcohol use. His lawyers challenged their relevance to the allegations, and material about treatment at a sex addiction clinic was omitted from a former assistant's evidence. Those disputes were separate from the agreement concerning Perry. The Crown Prosecution Service confirmed that investigators had not asked Perry for a witness statement. Senior Crown Prosecutor David Roberts said reasonable lines of inquiry relevant to the charges had been pursued. There is no basis in that statement to suggest Perry refused to cooperate. Katy Perry's Marriage Still Entered the Courtroom Perry and Brand began dating in 2009 and married in Rajasthan, India, in 2010. They separated in December 2011, and their divorce was finalised in 2012. The offences for which Brand was convicted took place between 2004 and 2009. During his evidence, Brand referred to the marriage and said it had brought him 'staggering fame'. The comment arose from his own testimony, not the prosecution's opening statement. It did not turn Perry into a witness or complainant. The Crown Prosecution Service said the women whose cases resulted in convictions came forward independently after a television investigation aired in September 2023. Prosecutors relied on their accounts and testimony from other witnesses to present evidence of Brand's conduct. Following the verdict, Roberts said Brand had 'used his celebrity status to commit sexual crimes'. The agency thanked the women for coming forward and stressed that sexual offences can be prosecuted years after they occur. The complainants have lifelong anonymity. Mr Justice Joel Bennathan refused Brand bail and remanded him in custody ahead of sentencing on Monday, 9 November. The judge warned that he faced a 'significant custodial term'. Rape carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment in England and Wales. © Copyright IBTimes 2026. All rights reserved.

title: En 2023 , Francisco organizó su sucesión : Puso a Prevost en el lugar idóneo por si soplaba el Espíritu Santo en esa dirección …
summary: Antes de escribir la biografía de Jorge Bergoglio, que llamó El gran Reformador, Austen Ivereigh ya era un experto en la historia de la Iglesia argentina. “Mi tesis de doctorado [en Oxford], que termi
content: Antes de escribir la biografía de Jorge Bergoglio, que llamó El gran Reformador, Austen Ivereigh ya era un experto en la historia de la Iglesia argentina. “Mi tesis de doctorado [en Oxford], que terminé en el 92, fue sobre catolicismo y política en la Argentina”. Y hay más: “Debo mi fe a la Iglesia Argentina, leyendo artículos de monseñor (Gustavo) Franceschi, volví a la fe”, dice. Ese conocimiento de nuestro país y de su fe mayoritaria representó una ventaja a la hora de escribir sobre Bergoglio, ya que cada etapa de la trayectoria del futuro Papa está debidamente contextualizada en la época que atravesaba el país. Desde aquel marzo de 2013, cuando la novedad de un pontífice argentino y jesuita impactó al mundo entero, Ivereihg siempre pensó que vendría cuando Francisco visitara la Argentina, viaje que finalmente no se concretó. “Ahora vengo con León”, comenta. En efecto, este escritor, historiador, periodista y analista de asuntos religiosos y políticos estará en nuestro país contemporáneamente con la visita del papa León XIV, invitado por la Universidad del Salvador (USAL), donde dictó, el pasado viernes 6, una clase magistral sobre “El giro latinoamericano Francisco-León: la Iglesia misionera sinodal y el cambio de época”. Ivereigh también es co-autor de Let Us Dream (Soñemos Juntos, 2020), un libro escrito en colaboración con Francisco. Su trabajo más reciente es First Belong to God: On Retreat with Pope Francis (Lo primero es pertenecer a Dios: Un retiro con el Papa Francisco, 2024), basado en los escritos y charlas de Bergoglio como director espiritual de un retiro ignaciano de 8 días. De 2004 a 2006, Ivereigh fue colaborador del entonces arzobispo de Westminster, cardenal Cormac Murphy-O’Connor, uno de los más activos promotores de la candidatura de Jorge Mario Bergoglio al papado. Ivereigh considera que el papado de Francisco inició un giro latinoamericano hacia una iglesia misionera y sinodal, cuyo primer paso fue la exhortación apostólica Evangelii Gaudium (noviembre de 2013), sobre “el anuncio del Evangelio en el mundo actual”, con la cual, dice, “Francisco inaugura una hoja de ruta de su Papado que también es la del pontificado de León”. Pero esa hoja de ruta tenía una génesis anterior: el ya famoso documento de Aparecida, la V Conferencia General del Episcopado Latinoamericano y del Caribe (Celam), redactado por Bergoglio. De esta manera, “América Latina pasó a ser la iglesia fuente”, señala, porque “siempre hay una parte de la Iglesia de la cual brota un dinamismo teológico”. Antes, ese rol lo cumplía Europa, pero a partir del Concilio Vaticano II eso cambia porque es en América Latina donde mejor se lo pone en práctica. Aclara que “fuente” no quiere decir centro; de hecho, “Francisco quería una Iglesia multipolar”. — ¿Hasta qué punto Aparecida refleja a Bergoglio como individualidad y hasta dónde es la Iglesia latinoamericana, que usted define como “fuente”? — El proceso de preparación de esa conferencia general, fue muy sinodal, de mucha consulta, y el papel de Bergoglio en esa conferencia general es muy conocido. Creo que influyó la recepción del Concilio Vaticano II en el Río de La Plata, que tuvo un matiz distinto al resto de América Latina. Tal vez, cuando llegó a Aparecida esa visión sobre la religiosidad popular estaba ya madura. Es decir, una teología de espiritualidad latinoamericana, distinta a anteriores teologías latinoamericanas. Bergoglio tenía muchas cosas que eran de él. Pero también llevaba en su forma de ser y de pensar muchos aportes de la iglesia argentina, la influencia de Lucio Gera y de Rafael Tello y toda esa tradición. — ¿Cómo vio el impacto de su papado en la Argentina? — Creo que una de las razones por las que no vino, sobre todo al principio, fue que tenía horror del triunfalismo. Y sabía que tal vez los argentinos tenían —todos los países lo tienen— una cierta tentación de decir: “El Papa es argentino”. title: 尼泊爾摩西計畫｜建設是器皿，傳福音、建立教會是目的
source: 中華宣教聯盟 · 宣教故事1001（中）
summary: 摩西計畫的唯一目的，就是傳福音、建立教會。從三期建設看見長期扎根的預備，並分清施工現況與未建規劃。
content: NEPAL · 摩西計畫 摩西計畫為什麼預備餐廳、接待空間與培訓基地？答案不是為了建築本身，而是為了福音能在尼泊爾扎根。 我們推動摩西計畫的唯一目的，就是傳福音、建立教會。 中華宣教聯盟・萬軍是回應耶穌基督大使命的宣教團隊。生活關懷、培訓與織帳篷工作，是長期與當地人同行的實際服事，並非取代這個使命的終點。 在尼泊爾，村莊教會與主日學、家庭探訪、青少年先修班和一對一真理造就，都是禾場服事報告所記錄的日常。這些人與教會的建立，才是我們理解基地預備的起點。 現地施工與設計願景，分開閱讀。 金白色室內畫面是裝修模擬，不是已完工照片；施工照片記錄拍攝當時的工程狀態。建設是器皿，傳福音、建立教會才是目的。 看四張精選影像與完整服事脈絡 → 三期建設，一個使命 第一期｜接待與生活場域 以婚紗攝影旅館、空中花園咖啡廳及相關空間、木工作品為主，呈現生活與接待場域逐步形成的歷程。 第二期｜婚宴餐廳與公共工程 Golden Himal Palace 婚宴大餐廳、和平塔，以及大門、信望愛噴泉與廣場等公共工程，都放在長期生活、接待與服事的脈絡中理解。工程資料中的現況影像與設計願景，必須分別標示，不能把模擬圖當成完工實景。 第三期｜培育與傳承的規劃 神學院、大旅館及學生宿舍等屬新建規劃。這些是未建工程的設計展示，不是落成照片，也不代表已確定施工或啟用日期。神學培育與生活預備，都要回到門徒生命、工人裝備與教會建立的方向。 從看見建築，到明白我們為何出發 我們盼望基地成為長期生活、接待、培訓與服事的器皿；真正看重的，不只是外觀與設備，而是人在真實相處中認識福音、生命被建立，教會能在當地扎根。 邀請你為尼泊爾的福音工作、前線同工與裝備培育守望。認識工程之前，也請先認識我們的使命： 傳福音，建立教會。 看摩西計畫與建設進程 → 認識尼泊爾教會、培訓與社區 → 本文依近期整理的三期工程展示資料與事工紀錄介紹方向；並非完工或營運啟用公告。

title: 2026 新竹宣教年會回顧｜宣教不是口號，而是走進生活
source: 中華宣教聯盟 · 宣教故事1001（中）
content: 2026 年 10 月 18 日，新竹宣教年會圓滿完成。 這次聚會沒有只談遙遠的國家，而是回到一個最重要的問題： 宣教如何進入真實生活？ 從陪伴孩子成長、在陌生城市建立關係，到幫助家庭靠自己的雙手站立起來，每一個禾場都提醒我們—— 福音不是短暫經過，而是長久同行。 三個現場，看見宣教正在發生 東馬 陪伴兒少，從一餐飯與一堂課開始 在缺少穩定教育資源的社區，生命中心持續以課程、餐食與日常陪伴守住孩子的成長。真正的改變不一定從大型活動開始，常常是有人願意每天在同一個地方等候。 寮國 從語言與社區關係，踏出開拓的第一步 新的禾場正在南部城市逐步扎根。同工透過語言學習、社區接觸與自立基地的預備，尋找能夠長期生活、服務鄰舍的方式。不是快速擴張，而是先聽懂土地與人的需要。 南蘇丹與非洲 培育青年，陪伴難民預備返鄉 難民不只需要眼前的救助，更需要重新建立家園的能力。門訓、教育、足球與生計訓練，都是陪伴青年找回方向、預備回到自己社區的重要一步。 年會影音｜用四段短片走近宣教現場 以下四段影片皆為網站壓縮版，可直接點選播放。 01｜教會・差會本為一家 02｜非洲難民返鄉計畫 03｜伊拉克・摩蘇爾生活基地 04｜尼泊爾・摩西計畫 「宣教不是一場活動的結束，而是一段同行的開始。」 謝謝每一位在禱告、服事與支持中同行的夥伴。邀請您繼續關心萬軍各地禾場的最新進展。 看更多宣教消息 參與支持與奉獻

title: 2026萬軍宣教年會 新竹場｜穆斯林歸主契機
source: 中華宣教聯盟 · 宣教故事1001（中）
summary: 「現在是宣教收割的季節，是華人回應大使命…
content: 「現在是宣教收割的季節，是華人回應大使命的關鍵時刻。」 若我們是支小蠟燭，就讓我們放在黑暗、困苦流離最需要的地方。 因為耶穌說：做在最小的弟兄身上，就是做在主身上。 新竹場・聚會資訊 日期 2026年10月18日 (日) 時間 14:00 – 16:00 地點 新竹勝利堂 (東區建功一路2號) 聯絡 林文欽牧師 (03-5257677) — 宣教前線分享焦點 — 東馬 ｜黑區無國籍流民 非洲 ｜百萬難民營呼聲 伊拉克 ｜福音在亞述的契機 尼泊爾 ｜密宗印度教之地 邀請您，成為同站立的禱告勇士 在前往新竹場之前，誠摯邀請您先透過上一場聚會的精華紀錄 一同感受聖靈的震撼與感動，點燃心中的宣教之火！ 觀看【高雄武昌教會】宣教年會回顧

title: 教會・差會本為一家｜2026 高雄武昌教會萬軍宣教年會回顧
source: 中華宣教聯盟 · 宣教故事1001（中）
summary: 2026 WANJUN MISSION …
content: 2026 WANJUN MISSION · KAOHSIUNG RECAP 教會・差會 本為一家 2026 高雄武昌教會萬軍宣教年會回顧｜在敬拜、分享與禱告中，再次回應走向萬民的呼召。 OCTOBER 7 · KAOHSIUNG 同心聚集，看見教會與禾場彼此相連 10 月 7 日晚間，弟兄姊妹在高雄武昌教會相聚。從敬拜、信息到禾場分享，整場聚會不只是一次事工報告，更是一個彼此提醒的時刻： 宣教不是少數人的遠方故事，而是教會一同領受、一同承擔的使命。 當眾人舉手回應、安靜禱告，也聆聽不同禾場仍在發生的故事，我們再次看見：每一份守望、每一次同行、每一個願意踏出的腳步，都能成為福音繼續向前的力量。 「教會與差會彼此連結，才能把所領受的使命，走成一條長久的路。」 DATE 2026 年 10 月 7 日 PLACE 高雄武昌教會 PHOTO STORY 精選影像紀實 — 一同敬拜，也一同回應 — 從信息出發，再次思想教會與宣教彼此同行的關係。 會眾在聚會中舉手回應，一同守望禾場。 不同年齡的弟兄姊妹一同投入敬拜與分享。 透過地圖與現場分享，看見宣教足跡彼此相連。 生命見證讓遠方的故事，成為眼底真實的同行。 從長期陪伴與生活扎根，看見禾場一步一步向前。 NEXT GATHERING 下一場，10 月 18 日新竹見 延續這份感動，邀請您走進第 4 場年會，一同聆聽、禱告並回應呼召。 前往【新竹場】聚會資訊

title: 從硬土到盼望｜伊拉克、尼泊爾與衣索比亞的生活宣教
source: 中華宣教聯盟 · 宣教故事1001（中）
summary: 從伊拉克滴灌果樹、尼泊爾摩西計畫，到衣索比亞 JOY 農場的拓荒記憶，看見萬軍如何在生活中學習、同行，使福音在硬土扎根。
content: WANJUN FIELD NOTES · 2026 在硬土上，把福音活成看得見的盼望 從伊拉克的滴灌果樹、尼泊爾摩西計畫的基地建設，到衣索比亞 JOY 農場留下的拓荒經驗；三片土地，見證同一個方向：進入生活、長久同行，使福音在當地扎根。 萬軍走進的禾場，常是環境艱難、資源有限，也少有人願意長期留下的地方。近期資料讓我們再次看見：宣教並不只發生在講台上，也發生在一條水管、一棵樹苗、一棟正在成形的建築，以及一次次不放棄的學習裡。 IRAQ · 伊拉克 讓乾旱土地重新長出盼望 近期農場以滴灌方式照顧近萬棵橄欖、葡萄等樹苗，整體存活率約七成五。下一階段將持續面對施肥、病蟲害與果實保護。這不只是農業成果，更是與社區建立信任、陪伴家庭走向穩定生活的一條路。 NEPAL · 尼泊爾 基地不是終點，而是承接生命的空間 奇旺約七公頃的摩西計畫基地持續推進，道路與地下管線等基礎工程已逐步完成，主要接待空間進入結構與細部施工階段；Golden Himal Palace 與多功能聚會空間則依現場條件分期規劃。工程的目的，是預備接待、培訓、退修與在地生計的平台。 ETHIOPIA · 衣索比亞 從一顆雞蛋開始的生活宣教 早年萬軍在衣索比亞建立 JOY 農場，引進生態養雞與發酵床技術，高峰期飼養逾三千隻雞，並由同工一家一家拜訪商店與餐廳，建立穩定的銷售關係。農場留下的不只是產業紀錄，更是一段學習在陌生文化中誠實工作、與人同行的拓荒歷史。 MISSION DNA · 萬軍的核心 生活就是宣教：不會的就學，會的彼此配搭 王老師常提醒同工，盡心盡力不是抽象口號。禾場需要農業，就學農業；需要水電與工程，就進到現場跟著專業師傅學。宣教士不是只把一篇信息帶到遠方，而是願意與當地人同吃、同住、同勞動，在最平凡的生活裡把基督的愛活出來。 「不會的就趕快去學；會的帶著不會的，彼此配搭。」 農場、建築、生計與慈善都很重要，但它們不是事工的終點。萬軍始終要問：這份投入是否真正承接生命、建立門徒，並使福音在當地成為能夠繼續傳承的根基？這也是衣索比亞的經驗，留給今天每一個禾場最深的提醒。 PRAY · PARTICIPATE · SUPPORT 請與我們一起守望 為伊拉克禱告 求主保守樹苗、農作與社區關係，使乾旱之地持續長出生命。 為尼泊爾禱告 求主賜下施工安全、智慧與合一，讓每個空間按真正需要成形。 為禾場同工禱告 求主使眾人忠心學習、彼此配搭，在生活中成為福音的見證。 認識伊拉克禾場 認識尼泊爾摩西計畫 認識衣索比亞禾場 資料整理至2026年9月30日。為保護前線安全，本文不公開同工姓名、精確位置、行程、醫療、財務及未定案資訊；工程進度以現場最新紀錄為準。

title: 2026萬軍年會高雄場｜所以，你們要去，使萬民作主的門徒
source: 中華宣教聯盟 · 宣教故事1001（中）
summary: 2026萬軍年會高雄場將於10月7日在高雄武昌教會舉行，邀請弟兄姊妹一同聆聽非洲、尼泊爾、寮國與東馬的前線宣教分享，回應主的大使命。
content: 大使命的呼召 「所以，你們要去，使萬民作我的門徒。」 —— 馬太福音二十八章19節 2026萬軍年會高雄場 把腳踏進神正在工作的地方・同心回應萬民的呼求 實體聚集・免費入場（備有愛宴） 距離年會聚集還有 00 天 00 時 00 分 00 秒 從最初順服呼召、踏出宣教的第一步，到今天持續走進非洲、尼泊爾、寮國與東馬等不同禾場，萬軍一次次看見： 宣教不只是少數人的遠方故事，而是全教會共同回應大使命的信心行動。 誠摯邀請弟兄姊妹一同前來，聆聽第一線宣教士帶來的真實見證，看見列國靈魂的迫切需要，並在深入的分享交流中，發掘神量給你在列國中的獨特位置。 聚會日期 2026年10月7日（星期三） 入場時間 下午6時開放入場（備愛宴晚餐） 聚集地點 高雄武昌教會 B1／一樓 聯絡專線 0937-877113 （春芬姊妹） 複製 PROGRAM 年會流程安排 18:00 – 18:30 開放入場・報到交流 武昌教會 B1 迎賓接待 18:30 – 19:30 愛宴晚餐團契 武昌教會 B1 餐廳，享受肢體溫馨相通 19:30 – 19:45 詩歌敬拜 齊心將眼光轉向榮美真神 19:45 – 20:00 宣教專題信息 主講： 郭俊豪 牧師 20:00 – 20:40 前線宣教區概況分享 非洲區 ｜ 林文欽 牧師 尼泊爾 ｜ 楊中生 牧師 寮國 ｜ 王世龍 牧師 東馬 ｜ 蔡宗勳 牧師 20:40 – 21:00 大會勉勵與總結 主講： 王老師 21:00 – 21:30 小組深入對話・共尋呼召 分組交流、代禱祝福、回應大使命 21:30 平安散會・差遣前行 在自己的位置上，與神同行 宣教可以從禱告守望開始，可以從甘心奉獻開始，可以用專業技能投入服事，也可以是勇敢踏出前往禾場的那一步。 願我們再次聽見主慈愛的呼召，讓福音走向萬民！ 主辦單位：萬軍團隊 協辦單位：高雄武昌教會、高雄策盟 支持宣教奉獻 點亮前線小蠟燭・同做神國後盾 更多最新消息 關注列國禾場動態與見證 電話已複製到剪貼簿 🎉

title: 我在這裡，請差遣我｜2026 台中場萬軍宣教年會回顧
source: 中華宣教聯盟 · 宣教故事1001（中）
summary: 2026 年 9 月 20 日，萬軍宣教年會在台中思恩堂美福教會舉行。這不只是一場禾場近況的分享，更是一個邀請：讓門徒訓練不只改變生命，也使人活出使命；從聽見遠方，到願意把自己放進神正在工作的地方。
content: 2026 WANJUN MISSION・TAICHUNG 我在這裡， 請差遣我 這不只是一場禾場報告，而是一個回應的邀請：從聽見遠方，到願意把生命放進神正在工作的地方。 2026 台中場萬軍宣教年會回顧 讓門徒訓練，不只改變生命，也使人活出使命 2026 年 9 月 20 日，我們在台中思恩堂美福教會相聚。從非洲、中東、黑海到南島，講台上的每一段分享，都不是遙遠的故事，而是正在發生的生命現場。 有人在艱難的環境裡長久陪伴，有人用教育與生活技能扶持一個家庭重新站起；也有人在受裝備之後，預備回到自己的家鄉建立教會。宣教因此不只是一趟旅程，而是一種被福音更新後的生活。 「我在這裡，請差遣我。」 宣教不是只把消息帶回來，而是讓台灣的教會看見：生命如何在長久陪伴中被建立。 從難民青年到返鄉的門徒 在生活裡接受裝備，也在生活裡預備被差遣 年會影片分享了難民青年接受一年裝備的過程：聖經、音樂、電腦、體育與生活技能一起進入每天的學習。訓練不是把信仰留在課堂，而是讓人學習承擔、服事，並在帳篷教會中實習。 當第一批學生預備回到家鄉，他們帶回去的不只是一份知識，更是一個建立教會、陪伴社區的使命。福音在這裡成為能夠走進家庭，也能夠走回故鄉的力量。 一張地圖讓遠方不再只是地名，也讓每一個禱告有了方向。 移動中的世代，也能成為被差遣的世代 把離開家鄉的路，轉化為帶著使命前行的路 在尼泊爾的分享中，青年大量前往海外工作，是家庭的盼望，也是當地教會長期面對的挑戰。好不容易建立的年輕門徒，可能很快就離開熟悉的土地。 但年會提出另一個眼光：如果門徒被健康地建立，他們不只是外出工作的人，也能在所到之處成為宣教士。流動不再只是失去，也可能成為福音跨越文化、進入新群體的道路。 ONE BODY・MANY FIELDS 四個區域，一個彼此承接的宣教身體 年會把非洲、中東、黑海與南島的工作放在同一個視野中。不同禾場有不同的語言、需要與節奏，但都指向同一件事：教會要在真實生活裡陪伴人，也要預備下一代接續前行。 非洲 難民青年裝備、社區陪伴與返鄉開拓 中東 在艱難之地以生活、產業與福音長久同行 黑海 面對變動與流離，建立能承擔使命的門徒 南島 跨越島嶼與文化，承接福音最後一棒 從聽見，到一起回應 敬拜、禱告，也讓每一個人說出自己的下一步 聚會的最後，不是停在「知道更多」。會眾一起敬拜、禱告，並在小組中分享與聆聽。有人重新看見自己的位置，有人開始為禾場守望，也有人思考：我能如何參與神已經開始的工作？ THE NEXT STEP 宣教從一個願意的回應開始 不是每一個人都立刻走到遠方，但每一個人都能開始聆聽、禱告、關心，並在神所託付的位置上踏出下一步。 認識萬軍宣教禾場 加入禱告與守望

content: 2026 WANJUN MISSION・TAICHUNG 把腳踏進 神正在工作的地方 不是只聽見遠方，而是一起看見福音如何在艱難之地開出道路。 9月20日（日） 14:00－16:30 查看完整邀請 一封來自禾場的邀請 2026 台中場萬軍宣教年會 從東馬、非洲、伊拉克到尼泊爾，四個禾場、四段仍在發生的生命故事。這一次，我們不只報告遠方的消息，更邀請您走近神正在工作的地方，看見福音如何在流離、貧乏與文化隔閡之中，繼續開出盼望的道路。 9月20日下午，讓我們在台中相聚。帶著一顆願意聆聽、禱告與回應的心，與萬軍一同看見、一同守望，也一同踏出下一步。 「當自己的腳甘心踏上苦難的道路，自由就成為獻上的選擇。」 DATE 2026年9月20日（日） TIME 報到 13:50｜聚會 14:00－16:30 PLACE 台中思恩堂美福教會 完整活動資訊 誠摯邀請您預留時間，與我們一同參與。

title: 2026 禾場近況｜從基地收尾到社區自立，六個禾場的穩健推進
source: 中華宣教聯盟 · 宣教故事1001（中）
summary: 2026 年六個禾場的可公開近況：尼泊爾工程收尾、寮國落腳評估、烏干達生活技能，以及伊拉克、緬甸、東馬的長期陪伴。
content: WANJUN FIELD UPDATE · AUGUST 2026 把進度寫清楚，也把前線安全守住 2026 年的禾場工作，不只是在地圖上增加一個點，而是讓基地、教育、生計與社區關係逐步成形。以下整理尼泊爾、寮國、烏干達、伊拉克、緬甸與東馬來西亞可公開的近況；人名、行程、證件、醫療與敏感位置不列入網站。 黑海區 尼泊爾｜工程進入收尾 道路依在地條件改採鋼筋混凝土，地下管線溝完成；大型聚會與接待空間依施工紀錄逐步整理。工程進度以現場紀錄為準，不把規劃寫成成果。 閱讀尼泊爾禾場 → 南島區 寮國｜先安頓，再發展 團隊先完成生活落腳，再評估土地、水源、雨季條件與小型農業方向。先學習文化、建立關係，才決定後續基地與生計規模。 閱讀寮國禾場 → 非洲區 烏干達｜培育連結生活技能 HOST 宣教學校持續陪伴青年，並把信仰培育、水資源、農業及小型養殖連結成可實踐的生活路徑，幫助所學能回到家庭與社區。 閱讀烏干達禾場 → 中東區 伊拉克｜基地走向長期陪伴 供水、圍護與種植條件逐步改善，團隊持續以家庭、社區及生活需要為起點，建立可長久同行、可被信任的服事。 閱讀伊拉克禾場 → 南島區 緬甸｜以教育連結家庭 學校持續以基礎教育、生活陪伴與家庭連結服事兒童；新的服務方向仍按安全、需要與在地承擔能力審慎推進。 閱讀緬甸禾場 → 南島區 東馬｜多點教育與社區陪伴 多個社區學習與陪伴據點持續運作；兒童教育、災後陪伴、家庭關懷與在地人才培育，正逐步連成一條長期路徑。 閱讀東馬禾場 → PRAY · PARTICIPATE · SUPPORT 你可以怎麼參與？ 禱告： 為在地同工、社區關係、教育與工程安全守望。 專業參與： 以教育、農業、建築、媒體或行政經驗成為長期夥伴。 奉獻支持： 讓基地、教育與生計計畫能按需要穩健推進。 資料整理至 2026 年 8 月。本文只公開可安全說明的事工方向與階段進度；未公開人名、精確位置、行程、證件、醫療、財務路線及未定案資訊。

title: 走進非洲難民中的服事——萬軍宣教工作的生命見證
source: 中華宣教聯盟 · 宣教故事1001（中）
summary: GOOD TV 國度新聞・非洲宣教專題 …
content: GOOD TV 國度新聞・非洲宣教專題 走進非洲難民中的服事——萬軍宣教工作的生命見證 透過實地拍攝、採訪與剪輯，GOOD TV 帶領觀眾走進萬軍在非洲的服事現場， 看見福音如何在艱難環境中成為盼望，也看見前方與後方同工彼此配搭的珍貴見證。 完整觀看｜GOOD TV 非洲萬軍事工精剪版 影片可直接在本頁播放 若您的瀏覽器無法顯示影片，可使用頁面下方的「前往 YouTube 觀看」按鈕。 近期，GOOD TV《國度新聞》連續播出萬軍在非洲服事的專題內容。 有了實地影像、採訪與完整剪輯，使我們能更深入地認識神所興起、所帶領的奇妙工作， 也能看見同工如何走進不同文化與艱難環境，在生命中陪伴、服事並傳遞盼望。 報導從華人宣教的整體路線出發，呈現萬軍多年來跨越地區與文化的腳步； 鏡頭也進入非洲現場，記錄宣教學校、敬拜、婦女關懷、家庭陪伴， 以及同工在日常生活中默默付出的真實樣貌。 現在正是宣教的季節。華人應當快快地起來，接棒福音使命， 在各自的崗位上彼此配搭，同心完成主所託付的工作。 從報導中看見萬軍的服事足跡 從華人出發，回應普世宣教使命 報導透過地圖整理萬軍長年累積的宣教路線。 這不只是一條地理上的移動軌跡，更代表許多同工跨越語言、文化與生活條件， 一步一步建立福音的接棒與服事平台。 透過媒體，讓更多人認識前線工作 GOOD TV 的採訪與剪輯，將分散於各地的服事內容整理成清楚的影像故事。 原本較難向外完整說明的工作，也因著新聞報導，被更多關心宣教的人看見與理解。 培育門徒，也建立同行的群體 宣教學校不只是知識與課程的傳遞，更是一段共同生活、敬拜、學習與成長的旅程。 同工在當地陪伴青年建立信仰根基，也預備他們成為能夠繼續服事別人的生命。 走進婦女與家庭，陪伴真實需要 萬軍的工作不只停留在大型聚會，而是進入家庭與日常生活。 透過婦女課程、關懷與長期陪伴，讓信仰的盼望落實在婚姻、家庭及社區關係中。 在病痛與限制中，仍然選擇留下服事 報導記錄 George 面對身體免疫系統問題與緊急就醫的經歷。 即使歷經病痛，他與妻子仍選擇留在非洲。 這份堅持不是英雄式的口號，而是在日常照顧與彼此扶持中，繼續走下去的真實信心。 崗位雖然不同，使命卻彼此相連 前方同工走進難民與社區，後方同工透過代禱、奉獻、行政與各種支持共同參與。 每一個崗位看似不同，卻都連結在同一個使命裡，成為這項工作得以持續的重要力量。 謝謝每一位同心守望與支持的同工 這個平台已經完成。感謝每一位代禱、關心、奉獻與支持萬軍的同工。 我們在這裡是一個身體、一個團隊，不分前方與後方； 願我們繼續彼此配搭，一起打這一場美好的仗。 前往 YouTube 觀看影片 ×

title: Pope Leo XIV declares Peru his homeland as he arrives in Lima on a historic visit

content: Pope Leo XIV described Peru as his âhomelandâ on Wednesday as he arrived in Lima for a historic visit, expressing gratitude to the people of the country for shaping his journey as a pastor through their experiences, struggles and joys. Addressing president Keiko Fujimori and government officials after his arrival, the Chicago-born pontiff said the Peruvian citizenship he received in 2015 had strengthened a connection that had existed long before. In an emotional speech, he acknowledged the deep personal bond he shared with the country, according to news agency AP. âToday I understand how much of this land remains with me and how much of my own story also belongs to you,â Leo said, drawing applause from those present. âThat is why I can tell you, with deep gratitude, that I am also returning to my homeland.â The pope received an enthusiastic welcome as he stepped off his chartered aircraft at Lima's airport, where he was greeted by Fujimori and embraced two children who presented him with flowers. According to the Vatican, nearly three million people lined the route of his motorcade into the capital, waving Peruvian and Vatican flags. Several enthusiastic supporters broke through security barriers to follow his vehicle as he travelled to the presidential palace for a private meeting with the president. During the formal welcome ceremony in the palace courtyard, Leo also sang the Peruvian national anthem alongside Fujimori and a children's choir. The Peru visit marks the final leg of the pope's three-country South American tour and its emotional high point. Before becoming pontiff, Leo, born Robert Prevost, spent more than two decades in Peru, serving as a missionary priest and later as a bishop. He has repeatedly credited the country with teaching him the meaning of pastoral leadership. Holding citizenship of both the United States and Peru, Leo is the first pope from either country. âWe love him so much because he's worked here, he knows our sufferings, he knows it all,â said 85-year-old Evelina Cruz, who waited for his arrival carrying a stuffed toy of the pope made by her niece. Peru welcomes its beloved 'Padre Robert' Excitement surrounding the pope's return was visible across the country. Ahead of his visit, a 14-metre statue of Leo was unveiled in the port city of El Callao, while cafes in Lima began serving cappuccinos featuring his image. âMy heart is so excited that it makes me want to cry with joy,â said Zuly Castillo, who previously worked as Leo's secretary when he served as bishop of Chiclayo in northern Peru. Gustavo Morello, an associate professor of sociology at boston college and author of lived religion in Latin America, described the visit as a return to the pope's roots. âPeru is the crown of the trip, the homecoming of the first Peruvian pope, no matter where he was born,â he said. Hundreds of people gathered outside the presidential palace in Lima, singing religious songs and chanting âLong live Christ!â as they awaited the pontiff. The enthusiasm has also spread to Chiclayo, where Leo is scheduled to arrive on Friday. Murals depicting the pope have appeared across the city, while his image features on T-shirts, baseball caps and bobblehead dolls. During the coming days, Leo is expected to visit several places associated with his years in Peru, including the sanctuary of St Turibius of Mogrovejo in ZaÃ±a, a centre of Afro-Peruvian culture. The pontiff frequently visited the sanctuary to pray to the saint, who holds a special place in his devotion. His familiarity with the country has heightened expectations surrounding his speeches, particularly an address scheduled for Thursday outside Lima's cathedral on the challenges and aspirations shaping Peru's future. Poverty, crime and political instability The pope's visit comes as Peru faces several pressing challenges, including economic inequality, violent crime, political instability and the looming threat of climate disruptions linked to El NiÃ±o. title: Pope Leo returns to a national celebration in his second homeland of Peru
summary: LIMA, Peru (AP) — Pope Leo XIV declared Peru his “homeland” on Wednesday as he arrived in Lima at the start of his historic visit, returning to the place that taught him how to be a pastor and where a
content: LIMA, Peru (AP) — Pope Leo XIV declared Peru his “homeland” on Wednesday as he arrived in Lima at the start of his historic visit, returning to the place that taught him how to be a pastor and where a nationwide party erupted to welcome the beloved “Padre Robert” home. Leo seemed genuinely moved as he emerged from his Aerolineas Argentinas charter plane, smiling broadly at nearly every turn of his first moments on Peruvian soil. The Vatican estimated that some 3 million people lined Leo’s kilometers-long (miles-long) motorcade route into town, waving Peruvian and Holy See flags. Some in the roaring crowds broke through the tight security to chase behind the car that transported him to the presidential palace for a meeting with Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori. During the formal welcome ceremony in the palace courtyard, the Chicago-born Leo sang the Peruvian national anthem alongside Fujimori and a children’s choir. In his first remarks to Fujimori and government officials, Leo said the Peruvian citizenship he acquired in 2015 cemented a bond that began long before, crediting Peruvians with having formed him as a pastor by sharing their lives, joys and struggles with him. “Today I understand how much of this land remains with me and how much of my own story also belongs to you,” he said. “That is why I can tell you, with deep gratitude, that I am also returning to my homeland,” he said to applause. The ceremony featured Indigenous Quechua music and a performance of the traditional Marinera dance from the northern coast of Peru and specifically Chiclayo, his former diocese. “The pope is Peruvian!” the crowd chanted as he arrived. The visit to Peru marked the final leg of Leo’s three-nation South America tour and its emotional highlight, given the more than two decades that the former Robert Prevost spent here as a missionary priest and later bishop. He has said it was here that he learned “what it means to be a shepherd.” “We love him so much because he's worked here, he knows our sufferings, he knows it all," said 85-year-old Evelina Cruz, who held a pope plush doll made by her niece as she waited for Leo to arrive. Elation over the pope's return felt across Peru In preparation for the pope’s visit, a huge 46-foot (14-meter) statue of the pontiff was unveiled in the port of El Callao. Baristas in Lima, the capital, were offering cappuccinos decorated with the image of the pope. “My heart is so excited that it makes me want to cry with joy,” said Zuly Castillo, who served as Leo’s secretary when he was bishop of the northern city of Chiclayo near the Pacific Coast. Gustavo Morello, an associate professor of sociology at Boston College and the author of “Lived Religion in Latin America,” said the trip was a “return to his origins, without any doubt.” “Peru is the crown of the trip, the homecoming of the first Peruvian pope, no matter where he was born,” he said. With hands raised and voices lifted in song, hundreds awaited the pope’s arrival in Lima in front of the presidential palace. “Long live Christ!” the crowd sang, following a Catholic choir on the stage. Popemania also hit Chiclayo, where Leo arrives on Friday. Leo is painted in colorful murals, emblazoned on T-shirts, baseball hats and even bobblehead dolls. Over the coming days, Leo will celebrate Mass in all his old stomping grounds including at the nearby sanctuary of St. Turibius of Mogrovejo in Zaña, a city that is a hub of Afro-Peruvian culture, and where the pope often visited to pray to the saint of his devotion. Since Leo knows his adopted country so well, his speeches will be closely watched, especially one he’ll deliver from the square in front of Lima’s cathedral Thursday “on the challenges and hopes for the future of the Peruvian people.” Peru hit by poverty and political instability Peru, a nation of 34 million people, is overwhelmed by challenges, among them the looming arrival of nature’s chaotic climatic agent El Niño, violent crime and income inequality

title: Papa León XIV regresa a Perú , el país donde desarrolló gran parte de su vida religiosa para una visita de seis días
summary: El papa León XIV llegó este miércoles a Perú para iniciar la última etapa de su gira por América Latina, en un viaje cargado de significado personal y religioso, debido al estrecho vínculo que mantien
content: El papa León XIV llegó este miércoles a Perú para iniciar la última etapa de su gira por América Latina, en un viaje cargado de significado personal y religioso, debido al estrecho vínculo que mantiene con esta nación sudamericana, donde vivió durante más de dos décadas y desarrolló gran parte de su trayectoria dentro de la Iglesia católica. La visita representa un reencuentro del pontífice con el país que considera parte fundamental de su historia personal y espiritual. En territorio peruano comenzó su labor como misionero, asumió posteriormente responsabilidades eclesiásticas de mayor importancia, llegó a convertirse en obispo y obtuvo la nacionalidad peruana. Después de cumplir compromisos en Uruguay y Argentina, León XIV permanecerá seis días en Perú, convirtiendo esta etapa en la más extensa de su recorrido sudamericano. Durante su estadía tiene previsto visitar Lima, Cusco, Pucallpa y Chiclayo, ciudades que forman parte de una agenda orientada a los encuentros religiosos, las actividades institucionales y el acercamiento con diferentes comunidades. Uno de los momentos más significativos del recorrido será su regreso a Chiclayo, donde ejerció como obispo durante ocho años, entre 2015 y 2023. En esa diócesis construyó importantes vínculos con la población y desarrolló una labor pastoral que dejó una huella en su trayectoria religiosa. UNA BIENVENIDA CON HONORES Y MUESTRAS DE CARIÑO El avión que trasladaba al Santo Padre desde Buenos Aires aterrizó a las 17:00 horas locales (22:00 GMT) en el aeropuerto internacional Jorge Chávez, ubicado en la provincia constitucional del Callao, que sirve a la capital peruana. A su llegada, el pontífice fue recibido por la presidenta de Perú, Keiko Fujimori, acompañada por el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores, Carlos Espá, quienes participaron en el acto oficial de bienvenida. La recepción estuvo acompañada de gestos de afecto y muestras de cercanía por parte de la población. Una pareja de niños entregó un ramo de flores al papa, mientras el coro infantil de Sinfonía por el Perú interpretaba una canción para darle la bienvenida. Este proyecto musical, impulsado por el tenor peruano Juan Diego Flórez, promueve la educación artística de niños y jóvenes, especialmente de aquellos que proceden de familias con recursos económicos limitados. En otro momento emotivo de la ceremonia, León XIV se apartó brevemente de la alfombra roja para acercarse a un grupo de menores huérfanos que viven en albergues estatales. El gesto permitió observar la cercanía del pontífice con los niños y su interés por saludar personalmente a quienes participaron en el recibimiento. AGENDA OFICIAL Y PRIMER MENSAJE A LOS PERUANOS Tras concluir las actividades en el aeropuerto, el papa se trasladará al centro histórico de Lima para sostener un encuentro con la presidenta Keiko Fujimori en el Palacio de Gobierno, donde también tendrá una breve audiencia con integrantes del gabinete ministerial. El recorrido hacia el centro de la capital incluirá un desplazamiento en el papamóvil por algunas de las principales calles del casco antiguo, permitiendo que los ciudadanos puedan observar y saludar al líder de la Iglesia católica durante su paso por la ciudad. La llegada a la Plaza Mayor de Lima será otro de los momentos destacados de la jornada, debido al significado histórico y político de este espacio, donde se encuentra la sede del Ejecutivo peruano.

title: Pope Leo returns to a national celebration in his second homeland of Peru
summary: LIMA, Peru (AP) — Pope Leo XIV declared Peru his “homeland” on Wednesday as he arrived in Lima at the start of his historic visit, returning to the place that taught him how to be a pastor and where a
content: LIMA, Peru (AP) — Pope Leo XIV declared Peru his “homeland” on Wednesday as he arrived in Lima at the start of his historic visit, returning to the place that taught him how to be a pastor and where a nationwide party erupted to welcome the beloved “Padre Robert” home. Leo seemed genuinely moved as he emerged from his Aerolineas Argentinas charter plane, smiling broadly at nearly every turn of his first moments on Peruvian soil. The Vatican estimated that some 3 million people lined Leo’s kilometers-long (miles-long) motorcade route into town, waving Peruvian and Holy See flags. Some in the roaring crowds broke through the tight security to chase behind the car that transported him to the presidential palace for a meeting with Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori. During the formal welcome ceremony in the palace courtyard, the Chicago-born Leo sang the Peruvian national anthem alongside Fujimori and a children’s choir. In his first remarks to Fujimori and government officials, Leo said the Peruvian citizenship he acquired in 2015 cemented a bond that began long before, crediting Peruvians with having formed him as a pastor by sharing their lives, joys and struggles with him. “Today I understand how much of this land remains with me and how much of my own story also belongs to you,” he said. “That is why I can tell you, with deep gratitude, that I am also returning to my homeland,” he said to applause. The ceremony featured Indigenous Quechua music and a performance of the traditional Marinera dance from the northern coast of Peru and specifically Chiclayo, his former diocese. “The pope is Peruvian!” the crowd chanted as he arrived. The visit to Peru marked the final leg of Leo’s three-nation South America tour and its emotional highlight, given the more than two decades that the former Robert Prevost spent here as a missionary priest and later bishop. He has said it was here that he learned “what it means to be a shepherd.” “We love him so much because he's worked here, he knows our sufferings, he knows it all," said 85-year-old Evelina Cruz, who held a pope plush doll made by her niece as she waited for Leo to arrive. Elation over the pope's return felt across Peru In preparation for the pope’s visit, a huge 46-foot (14-meter) statue of the pontiff was unveiled in the port of El Callao. Baristas in Lima, the capital, were offering cappuccinos decorated with the image of the pope. “My heart is so excited that it makes me want to cry with joy,” said Zuly Castillo, who served as Leo’s secretary when he was bishop of the northern city of Chiclayo near the Pacific Coast. Gustavo Morello, an associate professor of sociology at Boston College and the author of “Lived Religion in Latin America,” said the trip was a “return to his origins, without any doubt.” “Peru is the crown of the trip, the homecoming of the first Peruvian pope, no matter where he was born,” he said. With hands raised and voices lifted in song, hundreds awaited the pope’s arrival in Lima in front of the presidential palace. “Long live Christ!” the crowd sang, following a Catholic choir on the stage. Popemania also hit Chiclayo, where Leo arrives on Friday. Leo is painted in colorful murals, emblazoned on T-shirts, baseball hats and even bobblehead dolls. Over the coming days, Leo will celebrate Mass in all his old stomping grounds including at the nearby sanctuary of St. Turibius of Mogrovejo in Zaña, a city that is a hub of Afro-Peruvian culture, and where the pope often visited to pray to the saint of his devotion. Since Leo knows his adopted country so well, his speeches will be closely watched, especially one he’ll deliver from the square in front of Lima’s cathedral Thursday “on the challenges and hopes for the future of the Peruvian people.” Peru hit by poverty and political instability Peru, a nation of 34 million people, is overwhelmed by challenges, among them the looming arrival of nature’s chaotic climatic agent El Niño, violent crime and income inequality

title: Manta ray led marine scientist to lost fin
summary: By Mark Ellis — Growing up in Laguna Beach, California, Amber Sparks developed a deep love for the ocean, which led her to study marine science at UC Berkeley and earn a master’s degree at Scripps Institute in San Diego. As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, […]  The post  Manta ray led marine scientist to lost fin  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: By Mark Ellis — Amber Sparks (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) Growing up in Laguna Beach, California, Amber Sparks developed a deep love for the ocean, which led her to study marine science at UC Berkeley and earn a master’s degree at Scripps Institute in San Diego. As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, especially with the Rigs-to-Reefs program, when oil drilling platforms are decommissioned. “We work with the oil companies to repurpose certain parts of the platform, retrofit it so that it can remain in place and continue to function as an artificial reef,” she told God Reports. Amber’s work has taken her around the world, with many dive experiences and encounters in the ocean with marine life. But there is one story she will never forget. It happened in the Gulf of Mexico shortly after Amber graduated from Scripps Institute and was invited on a research industry cruise with oil company representatives, scientists, and regulators on a liveaboard vessel. At the Flower Garden National Banks, a marine protected area 200 miles offshore, Amber was excited about her first dive, but slightly nervous. “You don’t know what you’re going to see or what this experience is going to be like,” she recalls. Dropping in (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook) Each diver had to jump off the vessel to get in the water. “We’re all geared up with our snorkel, our buoyancy control device, our wetsuit, and fins are the last thing you put on. So, I put on my fins and I jumped off the side of the boat.” “The second that I hit the water, one of my fins fell off, and I looked down and watched as it slowly descended to the bottom.” Amber glanced over at her dive buddy, and said, “I’m gonna go down. I’m going down.” Normally she would wait for her dive partner and they would go down together, but in this case, she thought, “I can’t (wait). I gotta go get my fin.” So Amber slowly began to descend to the bottom, about 60 feet below the ocean surface. “I felt completely lost. I was in a completely new area. I never dove before, and now I only had one fin.” She realized there were major currents that could have moved her fin in any direction. “I realized I can’t really swim with just one fin. So now not only am I at depth, but I’m handicapped with just one fin, and I started to feel pretty nervous.” It would probably take her 10 minutes to get back the surface, with safety stops. At the moment before panic set in, she looked upward and saw an amazing sight. It was a giant manta ray, with wings extending at least 10 feet. “Its wingspan was double mine. Its arms were out, and it was coming up over the side of a reef. “I’ve never seen a manta ray like this before. It totally took my breath away, it was so magnificent.” Another manta ray (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) She noted that manta rays are known in the ocean community to be “majestic, God-connected creatures with an understanding maybe beyond what humans can fully comprehend. They see the world and feel it in another way,” she notes. Mantas have the largest known brain of any fish. Their brains are large in absolute terms and relative to body size, which is also true of elephants, dolphins, and people. Their brains have enlarged areas associated with intelligence, vision, and motor coordination, and some of their brain cells are more like those in birds and mammals than in other fish.(1) As the manta ray drew close to Amber, she had an unusual communication experience. “I felt this sense where it said, ‘I want you to follow me. I’m going to help you find your fin.’ Amber Sparks Amber’s diving partner had just descended next to her, and they both began to swim after the manta. “I was barely making it, following this manta ray across the reef. At this point, I was so excited to see a manta ray. I kind of forgot about being handicapped, and I was just trying to go as fast as I can to keep up with it. Then Amber got the sur

content: The word epiphany is defined by the Oxford Learner’s Dictionary as “a sudden and surprising moment of understanding.” Often, such epiphany moments arrive unexpectedly, interrupting the ordinary rhythms of life with extraordinary insight. Sometimes they come through a conversation, a passage of Scripture, or an encounter with nature. Other times, they emerge through art. Twilight Epiphany. Photo: Eliott Davis Sitting beneath artist James Turrell’s Twilight Epiphany on the campus of Rice University in Houston, Texas, on a Sunday morning as the sun rose, the word epiphany took on new meaning. As the morning light slowly illuminated the sky, subtle shifts in color transformed the space above me. The experience was both architectural and atmospheric, a convergence of art, nature, and contemplation. Turrell, born in 1943, is an American artist internationally recognized for his exploration of light, space, and human perception. Raised in the Quaker tradition, Turrell’s artistic vision reflects an appreciation for silence, stillness, and inward reflection. Commissioned by Rice University through the generosity of alumna Suzanne Deal Booth, Twilight Epiphany opened in 2012 as part of the university’s public art program. The pyramidal Skyspace, designed to accommodate approximately 120 visitors, features an aperture in its roof through which viewers observe the changing sky. At sunrise and sunset, carefully programmed LED lights interact with the natural atmosphere, creating an extraordinary experience of shifting color and perception. More than a work of architecture, the installation invites visitors to slow down, look upward, and reconsider the relationship between light and the world around them. James Turrell (Chat GPT) For me, the experience was something of a spiritual exercise. Light, after all, is among the Bible’s most enduring metaphors for divine revelation, truth, and beauty. As the colors shifted above me, I was reminded that beauty does not always announce itself loudly. Sometimes it simply asks us to be still and pay attention. Rothko Chapel. Photo: https://www.mark-rothko.org/rothko-chapel.jsp#google_vignette. From Rice University, I headed to another meditative landmark: the Rothko Chapel . Here, I sat among the monumental, dark-hued paintings of Mark Rothko, contemplating both the tragedy of the artist’s life and the triumph of the chapel that bears his name. Commissioned by Houston philanthropists John and Dominique de Menil in 1964 and dedicated in 1971, the Rothko Chapel is an interfaith sanctuary devoted to contemplation, spiritual reflection, and human rights. Its octagonal interior contains fourteen large-scale paintings by Rothko, whose subtle variations of black, maroon, and purple create an atmosphere of profound stillness. Rothko, born Marcus Rothkowitz in 1903, was a leading figure in American Abstract Expressionism, celebrated for his ability to evoke deep emotional responses through color and form. Yet his personal life was marked by physical illness, depression, and emotional turmoil. In February 1970, before the chapel’s dedication, Rothko died by suicide at the age of sixty-six. He never witnessed the completed sanctuary that would become one of his most enduring artistic legacies. Twilight Epiphany. Photo: Brian C. Nixon There is something deeply moving about this juxtaposition. An artist whose life ended in despair left behind a place where countless visitors have sought peace, meaning, and solace. The darkness of Rothko’s paintings does not necessarily communicate hopelessness. Rather, their quiet intensity invites viewers to confront the depths of human experience—sorrow, longing, mystery, and perhaps even transcendence. Where Turrell’s Twilight Epiphany draws the eyes upward toward the heavens, Rothko’s chapel seems to draw the gaze inward, toward the mysteries of the human soul. summary: While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence […]  The post  Lanier’s Sixth Annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series: A Grand Success  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: John Warwick Montgomery While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence with C. S. Lewis and his barrister gowns to the thousands of books that comprise his remarkable personal collection, Lanier has provided the Christian world with a marvelous tribute to one of the great Christian intellectuals of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. Born in 1931, John Warwick Montgomery (d. 2024) was a distinguished Christian apologist, theologian, attorney, and scholar whose extraordinary career spanned several disciplines. Holding numerous academic degrees, including doctorates in theology, philosophy, and law, Montgomery became internationally recognized for his defense of Christianity through historical evidence, legal reasoning, and philosophical argumentation. His influential books, including History and Christianity , Faith Founded on Fact , and The Shape of the Past , helped establish a rigorous approach to Christian apologetics. Whether lecturing in universities, debating skeptics, or practicing law, Montgomery maintained that Christianity was not merely a matter of subjective belief but a faith grounded in historical reality and rational inquiry. Yet to stop at the library would be to understate Lanier’s remarkable work. The sixth annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series was a tour de force of distinguished thinkers, passionate Christians, and intellectually engaging presentations. More than a commemoration of Montgomery’s life, the gathering represented a continuation of his intellectual legacy: the conviction that Christianity can withstand serious scrutiny and offer compelling answers to life’s most profound questions. Mark Lanier, Nancy Pearcey, Paul Gould, Adam Francisco, and Michael Horton From the opening panel discussion hosted by attorney and philanthropist Mark Lanier to Dr. Paul Gould’s thoughtful presentation on worldviews, followed by attorney Craig Parton’s lecture on jurisprudential apologetics, one theme emerged with unmistakable clarity: Christianity is a reasonable faith. The presentations reflected Montgomery’s own interdisciplinary approach to apologetics: the Christian faith and intellectual inquiry need not be adversaries. Indeed, the Christian tradition has long insisted that faith and reason are complementary avenues in the pursuit of truth. The following day continued this rich intellectual exploration. Professor Nancy Pearcey addressed questions surrounding truth, dismantling various modern ideologies, while Dr. Adam Francisco offered an informative overview of Islamic history and belief, helping participants better understand one of world’s biggest religions. The keynote address by Dr. Michael Horton examined the challenge of reaching those who identify as “spiritual but not religious,” a growing segment of contemporary society. Horton’s presentation underscored the importance of communicating historic Christian truth in a culture increasingly suspicious of religious institutions yet often deeply interested in spiritual meaning. Dr. Michael Horton On Sunday morning, Lanier founder, Mark Lanier, hosted many participants during his Biblical literacy class, where he continued the dialogue with Michael Horton. Taken together, the lectures, discussions, and interviews demonstrated the breadth of Christian scholarship and the continuing relevance of thoughtful apologetics in an age of skepticism, religious pluralism, and cultural uncertainty. summary: What do Jesus and Isaiah have in common? Quite a bit, according to renowned British New Testament scholar N. T. Wright. Gathering at the marvelous Lanier Theological Library in Houston, Texas—the brainchild of noted attorney, author, and biblical scholar Mark Lanier—Wright offered a packed house in the Great Room a fascinating glimpse into the relationship […]  The post  N. content: What do Jesus and Isaiah have in common? Quite a bit, according to renowned British New Testament scholar N. T. Wright. Gathering at the marvelous Lanier Theological Library in Houston, Texas—the brainchild of noted attorney, author, and biblical scholar Mark Lanier—Wright offered a packed house in the Great Room a fascinating glimpse into the relationship between the Old Testament prophet Isaiah and the life, ministry, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. Dr. Joseph Holden of Veritas International University listening to Dr. NT Wright at Lanier Library. For Wright, Isaiah is far more than an ancient prophetic voice whose words occasionally appear in the New Testament. Rather, the prophet provides a theological framework for understanding Jesus and the unfolding purposes of God. In his book Into the Heart of Isaiah , Wright invites readers to rediscover the extraordinary depth of Isaiah’s prophetic vision, demonstrating how its themes of judgment, restoration, redemption, and new creation find their ultimate expression in Christ. Central to Wright’s interpretation is the conviction that Isaiah’s message cannot be separated from the larger story of Israel. The prophet speaks of exile and homecoming, divine judgment and covenant faithfulness, suffering and salvation. These themes, Wright argues, become essential to understanding how Jesus understood his own mission and how the earliest Christians interpreted his life. Particularly significant is Isaiah’s portrayal of the suffering servant, whose affliction becomes the means through which God’s redemptive purposes are accomplished. Wright connects this prophetic imagery to Jesus’ sacrificial death, while emphasizing that the cross cannot be isolated from the broader biblical promise of God’s restoration of creation. Equally important is Isaiah’s vision of a renewed world, a creation in which justice, righteousness, and peace flourish under God’s reign. For Wright, the resurrection of Jesus announces the beginning of that promised new creation. The Christian hope, therefore, is not simply an escape from the present world, but the ultimate renewal of God’s good creation. Personal Stories: Mounting Up with Wings Like Eagles Amid the theological insights and biblical exposition, Wright shared several personal stories, offering the audience a glimpse into how the words of Isaiah have shaped not only his scholarship but also his spiritual imagination. One story centered on the beloved passage from Isaiah 40:31, in which the prophet declares that those who wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength and mount up with wings like eagles. Wright recalled preaching on Isaiah many years earlier and drew an amusing comparison to the long-running British radio program Desert Island Discs , in which notable guests select the recordings they would take with them if stranded on a deserted island. “I’ve sometimes said I have a set of desert island texts,” Wright explained, suggesting that certain biblical passages remain especially meaningful throughout one’s life. Near the top of his list, he said, is the closing portion of Isaiah 40, with its magnificent image of soaring eagles. The passage, he suggested, is more than a favorite theological text. It is part of his personal testimony, a biblical promise that has accompanied him through the years. A second story brought the imagery of Isaiah into an unexpected encounter with the natural world. While completing the final proofreading of Into the Heart of Isaiah , Wright and his wife, Maggie, were staying at their home in Scotland. Wright was alone in a room, carefully reviewing the text, when something outside caught his attention. “Out of the corner of my eye, I saw something,” he recalled. “At first, I thought it was somebody’s dog that had come into our front garden.” Noted Biblical archeologist, Dr. Steven Collins, listening to Mark Lanier interview Dr. NT Wright at Lanier Library. content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .

title: In the shadow of western stars: Grover Lewis, Larry McMurtry, and the triumph of words
summary: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star, the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of […]  The post  In the shadow of western stars: Grover Lewis, Larry McMurtry, and the triumph of words  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star , the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of one of America’s most celebrated novelists. Having written about McMurtry’s faith—or lack thereof—in a previous article , following an earlier visit to Archer City, I’m returning with a somewhat different interest. This time, my attention turns to Grover Lewis, the gifted journalist, critic, and poet whose life intersected with McMurtry’s during their college years. Lewis’ story, however, begins not with literary achievement but with almost unimaginable tragedy. As a child, he experienced the devastating loss of both parents when his father murdered his mother and was subsequently shot with the same gun, either by his dying wife or another person present. Lewis was only eight years old. It is difficult to imagine a more horrific beginning. Yet rather than allowing that tragedy to become the entirety of his story, Lewis eventually found a voice through literature. Perhaps the cards life dealt him gave him plenty to write about. Or perhaps writing became his way of making sense of a world that had revealed its cruelty far too early. In his autobiographical poem “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis writes: “You asked me once, Ann/Over coffee gone cold with talk/In your mother’s rain-drowsy/House, who they were, how it/Was with them in their breathless/Time in the wilds of years.” For Lewis, those early years were indeed wild. But they were also the soil from which his literary imagination would eventually grow. A Life in Words Born in Texas in 1934, Grover Lewis emerged as a distinctive voice in American journalism, particularly through his cultural criticism and reporting on the rapidly changing landscape of the 1960s and 1970s. He became known for his sharp observations, literary flair, and ability to capture the personalities and contradictions of American culture, even if he occasionally stretched the truth in the telling. His work appeared in prominent publications, including Rolling Stone , where his reporting helped establish his reputation as an insightful, sometimes cutting observer of popular culture. Lewis was more than a journalist, however. He was a poet and literary craftsman, someone who understood that words could do more than convey information. They could illuminate the human condition, expose its contradictions, and perhaps even provide a measure of healing. Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) Continuing “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis ponders: “At last, breathless and dry-mouthed/With private desire in the blue,/Swollen dark, we all lie down together—/My mother, my father, their perishing/Dreams, and I this unborn prisoner son…” There is something haunting about these lines. The dead remain present. The past refuses to disappear. And the poet, even as an adult, seems to wrestle with the circumstances that shaped his entrance into the world. Yet the very act of writing suggests something else: a refusal to remain silent. Two Texans, Two Literary Paths Lewis and Larry McMurtry crossed paths as students at North Texas State College, now the University of North Texas, during the 1950s. Both were young Texans drawn to literature and the possibilities of the written word. Their friendship developed within a shared intellectual environment, one that encouraged reading, conversation, and the pursuit of literary ambitions. Although their careers eventually followed different paths—McMurtry toward novels, screenplays, and literary fame, Lewis toward journalism, poetry, and cultural criticism—they shared an interest in the complexities of American life. summary: By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). content: Pastor Peter Colon portraying Major Rossvally in the movie of his story By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own life. For the 17-year-old Drummer Boy – too young for frontline duty – refused chloroform or brandy to dull the pain. Charlie Coulson chose instead to trust in Jesus, his Lord and Saviour. The doctor – an army major and Orthodox Jew – was understandably stunned by the boy’s bravery, as well as his boldness in declaring his faith in Christ and imploring the officer (whom he knew to be Jewish) to put his own trust in Jesus, since he was also the Jewish Messiah. Max, however, was shaken rigid, and in a great dilemma, as he had always been taught to hate Jesus. For his people had largely rejected him as an ‘impostor’ and false Messiah. Charlie died just days later, apparently more concerned for the doctor’s eternal destiny than for his own painful exit from this life. Ten years later, Max found himself in a barber’s chair in New York once more being urged to trust in Jesus. Having explained the gospel, the barber promised to pray for him and said that, whenever he came in contact with a Jew, he felt it his duty to introduce him to the one who came for “the lost sheep of Israel” (Matthew 10:6). The surgeon subsequently boarded a train for a business meeting in Washington, where a newspaper advertisement drew him to a ‘revival’ service where the preacher echoed the messages he had heard from the barber and the boy soldier, leaving him in tears. He agonised at home in prayer for some time afterwards, struggling most of all with the thought that, if he accepted Christ, he would be going against all the advice and teaching he had known, not to mention the Jewish community as a whole. But he finally became convinced that Jesus was indeed the fulfilment of Old Testament prophecies (in particular, Genesis 49:10, Micah 5:2 and Isaiah 7:14). So he prayed: “O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You know I am sincere in this thing. If Jesus Christ is the Son of God, reveal him to me this night, and I will accept him as my Messiah.” A long battle ensued, but his doubts were eventually replaced by joy and happiness as he praised God that he had found the true Shiloh, Ruler of Israel and Emmanuel. He was to pay a high price, however, as do all who follow Christ. His wife walked out on him; his parents disowned him. But he never gave up hope as he constantly prayed and reached out to his family. After 54 days, his wife joined him as a disciple of Jesus and, in time, his daughter also became a believer. But his son disowned him for many years until he was eventually reconciled both with his earthly and heavenly Father. In an extraordinary sequel some 18 months after he came to Christ, Max met up with Mrs Coulson, the mother of his dying young patient all those years earlier on the battlefield. With great joy, he was able to share how her son had set him on the path to a glorious future in Christ, which was to touch lives across the world, including my home county of Yorkshire in England. In fact, he came to live in Leeds to reach out to the Jewish community there and is buried at Lawnswood Cemetery in the city. An Irish friend of mine, Colin Nevin, has visited the grave, which includes an excerpt from one of the doctor’s hymns, I am Coming Soon, and was able to give a copy of Max’s story to a caretaker, so continuing the evangelist’s legacy more than a century after his death in 1892, aged 64. A 54-minute movie – Rossvally: From the Synagogue to the Saviour – has been produced on DVD and can apparently be ordered online.
